author: reek
body: write-file answers whether the write landed, and that answer is the whole reason it returns Boolean rather than Nothing: the disk can be full, the root directory can be full, and a subdirectory target is refused outright while the parent-directory walk is unwritten. Every one of those is ordinary. So the answer is read here rather than dropped -- a save that failed leaves the buffer dirty and says so, because a buffer marked clean over a write that never landed is the editor throwing the author's work away and reporting success. That is precisely what the old write-file builtin did before it was deleted, and it is not worth reinventing one layer up.

author: reek
body: Writer-role surface (H2). The cursor is a coordinate in source; author-annotation lifts that coordinate to a definition target, builds an Annotation, signs it via KeyManager, and stores both the plain annotation in AnnotationFact (read by CodeBrowser at H1) and the SignedAnnotation alongside (kept on the editor for later publish via H7). No outbound, no trust check yet.

author: reek
body: Of the queued payloads, the relevant subset for the editor is those whose target-chapter matches the file open in the editor. file-path-to-chapter is a heuristic -- it strips the directory and the .codex suffix.

author: reek
body: Three render shapes per Damian's framing -- throbber (subtle status-line dot), toast (auto-dismissing overlay), overlay (modal-ish review panel). The driver chooses based on user preference; this chapter just emits widget trees.

author: reek
body: H10: the annotator-side counterpart to H8. When a verdict arrives on a proposal this editor authored, surface it. The user can fetch the superseding fact or show a diff; both are queued as PendingAction values and consumed by the driver.

author: reek
body: fetch-new-fact and show-diff are queue-only here. The driver dequeues with take-pending-actions and dispatches to repo + transport. The editor doesn't know about TCP or disk; it only knows it wanted to do something with a proposal-id.
